Subject: Post-call: Aurora deployment priorities and gating criteria

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on how the deployment conversation should progress.

Key priorities you shared
- Identity: Okta SAML/SCIM integration required for workforce SSO + groups for role-based access.
- Key management: Production workload must use HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 level) for patient data; PoC can use non-HSM keys if isolated.
- Logging & retention: Audit logs must be retained for 5–7 years depending on dataset (PHI audit trails target 7 years); logs should be exported to your Splunk instance and to an immutable audit store.
- Data residency: US-East only for production; PoC may run in a shared US region if encrypted at rest.

Immediate implications
- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted) will be simplest for speed, but cannot meet the HSM requirement or strict log-export/residency model without migration to a private arrangement.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) can often meet the majority of your constraints if we place instances in a peered VPC and integrate with your KMS/CloudHSM, but we need to validate network topology and key access model.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is the “cleanest” fit for HSM + long-term log retention + full control over keys and egress, but involves additional operational steps and timeline.

Ask of Aurora: two quick clarifications to accelerate technical planning
1) Is HSM required for the PoC environment or only for production?
2) Can you share a pointer to your KMS architecture (AWS KMS vs CloudHSM vs vendor HSM) and whether you allow external services to call your KMS via peering / private link?
3) Who from procurement/security should we loop in for MSA / SOC2 / KMS assurances?

Attached: mutual action plan (Aurora_MAPlan_v2.pdf) and a starter Dedicated config CSV (redwood-dedicated-config.csv) that maps the variables we'll need to confirm.

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive with Ben & Karthik (30–45m) to validate KMS and logging flows — propose Tue Sep 7 or Wed Sep 8, two slots in the Doodle linked below.
- If PoC can accept non-HSM keys, proceed with a Dedicated PoC to validate latency and integration, then migrate production to Private VPC if HSM is required.

Thanks — I’ll hold the two slots pending confirmation.

Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap. A few answers and context from my side:

1) HSM requirement: Production must be HSM-backed for any key that decrypts PHI. For the PoC we can use KMS-managed keys (non-HSM) provided the environment is isolated and access-controlled. So PoC with Dedicated is acceptable if we can lock down networking and RBAC.
2) KMS architecture: we run AWS KMS + CloudHSM for our most sensitive keys. We prefer CloudHSM for production HSM-backed keys. We can consider exposing KMS calls to a peered service via PrivateLink but procurement/security will need the architecture doc to sign off.
3) Logs / retention: PHI audit trails need 7 years; other logs 5 years. We send audit streams to Splunk and also snapshot to an immutable archive in S3 (governed).

Procurement note: our procurement team prefers Dedicated hosting if it meets our KMS/HSM and data residency requirements; Private VPC is the fallback if Dedicated can’t satisfy the HSM integration.

I’ve copied Tom (infrastructure) for network topology — he can share the VPC layout if you need it. I’ll introduce procurement once we have a recommended technical pathway.

Alyssa Cheng

Thanks — quick technical readout from the infra/solutions side. High level: we can support both Dedicated and Private but there are tradeoffs.

Option A — Redwood Hosted API
- Pros: fastest to stand up for a quick demo.
- Cons: cannot meet CloudHSM-backed key requirements or long-term immutable log export under your control. BYOK for Hosted still requires transfer of key material or use of a remote KMS bridge which procurement typically rejects for HSM requirements.

Option B — Dedicated (our reserved capacity)
- We can place Dedicated instances in a peered VPC and configure private networking to access your AWS KMS and CloudHSM. For CloudHSM-backed keys used by the inference engine, we typically require either (1) a cross-account CloudHSM cluster in your account that the Dedicated cluster can talk to over VPC peering, or (2) a proxy model where KMS calls are brokered through a customer-owned endpoint. Both are possible but require network and key access approvals.
- Log export: Dedicated can stream audit logs directly to your Splunk via a forwarder in the peered VPC; retention policies are then handled on your side.

Option C — Private VPC / On-prem
- Full control: HSM in your environment, full log control, data residency. Longer lead time (ops + networking + onboarding) but minimal architectural gaps for production.

Recommendation for Aurora
- Start PoC on Dedicated with KMS-managed keys (non-HSM) to validate model performance, latency, and integration points. This gives a fast path for evaluation while we parallel-design the CloudHSM integration for production.
- Parallel work: Karthik and I will draft the CloudHSM integration pattern and a network checklist for your infra team. If procurement requires absolute HSM separation before any live testing, we’ll plan a Private VPC timeline instead.

Deliverables I will produce by next Tue (Sep 7):
- Dedicated PoC configuration example (resource sizes, network ports, required NAT/peering) — attached template referenced in Vanessa’s note.
- CloudHSM integration pattern doc (how keys are referenced by the runtime, latency considerations, failover).

Cc’ing Alyssa / Tom so they see the recommended path — happy to jump on the tech call and go through the checklist.
